name: Binary Search
description: Efficient search algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
requirements: Input array/list must be sorted in monotonic order
best_use_cases: Searching in large sorted numerical arrays
limitations: Requires data to be pre-sorted or sorted on insertion
Not directly suitable for linked lists due to lack of random access

name: Linear Search
description: Sequential search algorithm that checks every element in a list one by one until a match is found or the end is reached.
requirements: None (works on unsorted or arbitrary data)
best_use_cases: Single-pass searches where sorting cost exceeds search cost
limitations: Inefficient for large datasets

name: Hash Table / Dictionary Lookup
description: Data structure that stores key-value pairs using a hash function for near-constant time lookups and insertions.
requirements: Keys must be hashable and immutable
limitations: Unordered data storage
Hash collision handling overhead

name: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm
description: Graph search algorithm that solves the single-source shortest path problem for a graph with non-negative edge weights.
problem_patterns: min cost path non negative weights
requirements: Graph edge weights must be non-negative
best_use_cases: Road network navigation and GPS mapping
limitations: Fails or loops endlessly with negative edge weights

name: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
description: Traverses or searches graph/tree data structures layer-by-layer, finding shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
requirements: Unweighted graph or uniform step cost
best_use_cases: Shortest path in unweighted graphs or grids
limitations: High memory consumption for high-branching graphs

name: Depth-First Search (DFS)
description: Explores graph or tree branches as deep as possible before backtracking.
requirements: Visited tracker to prevent infinite loops in cyclic graphs
best_use_cases: Solving mazes and puzzles via backtracking
limitations: Does not guarantee shortest path in graphs

name: Quick Sort
description: Divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that partitions an array around a chosen pivot element.
requirements: Random or median-of-three pivot selection recommended
time_complexity: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst case
limitations: Unstable sort; worst-case O(n^2) on poorly chosen pivots

name: Merge Sort
description: Stable divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that divides arrays into sub-arrays, sorts them, and merges them.
requirements: Requires O(n) auxiliary space for arrays
limitations: Requires extra memory for temporary merge arrays

name: Two Pointers Technique
description: Algorithmic pattern using two indices to iterate through a data structure simultaneously, typically from both ends or at different speeds.
requirements: Data structure usually needs to be sorted or sequentially ordered
limitations: Applies primarily to linear sequential memory structures

name: Sliding Window Technique
description: Maintains a dynamic or fixed range (window) over a sequential array or string to evaluate subarray properties efficiently.
requirements: Problem requires contiguous subarray or substring evaluation
best_use_cases: Fixed or variable size contiguous subarray problems
limitations: Only applies when elements are contiguous

name: Dynamic Programming (DP)
description: Optimization method that solves complex problems by breaking them down into overlapping subproblems and storing subproblem solutions.
requirements: Optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems
limitations: High memory usage if state space is large

name: Logistic Regression
description: Linear classification algorithm that models the probability of a discrete target outcome using a logistic sigmoid function.
requirements: Features should be scaled; target must be categorical/binary
best_use_cases: High interpretability requirements with feature odds ratios
limitations: Assumes linear decision boundary between classes
python_template:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

name: Random Forest Classifier
description: Ensemble learning method that constructs a multitude of decision trees during training and outputs the mode of class predictions.
requirements: Tabular dataset with numerical or encoded categorical features
time_complexity: O(k * n * log n * d) training
limitations: Slower inference than single decision trees; larger model size
python_template:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

name: XGBoost Classifier
description: Optimized distributed gradient boosting library designed to be highly efficient, flexible, and accurate on tabular ML tasks.
requirements: Categorical variables encoded as numeric integers or one-hot vectors
time_complexity: O(k * n * log n * d) training
best_use_cases: State-of-the-art predictive performance on tabular data
Large tabular classification and regression datasets
limitations: Requires careful hyperparameter tuning to prevent overfitting
python_template:
from xgboost import XGBClassifier

model = XGBClassifier(n_estimators=100, eval_metric='logloss')
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

name: Decision Tree Classifier
description: Non-parametric supervised learning method that splits data based on feature thresholds creating a tree of decision rules.
requirements: Numerical or integer encoded categorical data
best_use_cases: Simple rule extraction and transparent decision logic
limitations: Prone to high variance and overfitting without pruning
python_template:
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier

model = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=5)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

name: Support Vector Machine (SVM / SVC)
description: Finds a hyper-plane in an N-dimensional space that distinctly classifies data points with maximum margin.
requirements: Features MUST be standardized/scaled
best_use_cases: Small to medium sized complex classification datasets
limitations: Scales poorly to datasets with >50,000 samples
python_template:
from sklearn.svm import SVC

model = SVC(kernel='rbf', probability=True)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
preds = model.predict(X_test)

name: Collaborative Filtering Recommendation
description: Recommendation system technique that predicts user preferences based on past interactions of similar users (User-User or Item-Item).
requirements: User interaction matrix (ratings, clicks, or views)
best_use_cases: Movie, music, and e-commerce product recommendations
limitations: Cold-start problem for new users/items with no ratings
python_template:
# Conceptual User-Item Matrix Factorization
from sklearn.decomposition import NMF

nmf = NMF(n_components=10)
user_features = nmf.fit_transform(user_item_matrix)
item_features = nmf.components_

name: Content-Based Recommendation
description: Recommends items to a user based on the similarity between item descriptions/attributes and the user's historical profile.
requirements: Rich item metadata and feature representations
best_use_cases: Overcoming cold-start for new items with detailed metadata
limitations: Tends to over-specialize and lack serendipity in recommendations
python_template:
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

similarity_matrix = cosine_similarity(item_tfidf_matrix)

name: Transformer / BERT NLP Classifier
description: Deep learning attention-based transformer model pre-trained on text corpora for contextual text understanding and classification.
requirements: GPU memory recommended for fine-tuning
best_use_cases: State-of-the-art text classification and sentiment analysis
Complex natural language parsing and context extraction
limitations: Computationally heavy; quadratic memory scaling with sequence length L
python_template:
# HuggingFace Transformers pipeline
from transformers import pipeline

classifier = pipeline('text-classification', model='distilbert-base-uncased')
result = classifier('Your text here')

name: K-Means Clustering
description: Unsupervised clustering algorithm that partitions n observations into k clusters in which each observation belongs to the cluster with the nearest mean.
requirements: Number of clusters k must be specified; features scaled
best_use_cases: Image quantization and color palette reduction
limitations: Sensitive to initial centroid placement and spherical cluster assumptions
python_template:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X)
